key_insight: Time-series foundation models scale: a single training recipe yields consistent forecast-quality improvements across model sizes from 4M to 2.5B parameters. The Toto 2.0 family (five open-weight models) sets new state-of-the-art results on BOOM, GIFT-Eval, and the contamination-resistant TIME benchmark.
problem_solved: Addresses the absence of a scalable, reliable foundation-model approach for time-series forecasting — eliminating uncertainty about whether increasing model size will improve accuracy and improving robustness to contaminated/observability-challenged data.
method: Design and apply a single, repeatable training recipe and architecture family across five model scales (4M → 2.5B parameters).
Train on diverse time-series corpora and evaluate extensively on BOOM (observability), GIFT-Eval (general-purpose), and TIME (contamination-resistant) benchmarks.
Release five open-weight models (Toto 2.0 family) and compare performance to establish new SOTA across benchmarks.
impact: Provides practitioners predictable scaling behavior for forecasting models and ready-to-use open weights that improve accuracy and robustness in production time-series tasks. Simplifies model selection, transfer, and deployment for observability and general forecasting use cases.
visual_elements: Scaling curve: x-axis = model parameters (4M → 2.5B), y-axis = forecast metric (improvement trend line).
Benchmark bar chart: side-by-side comparison of Toto 2.0 vs prior SOTA on BOOM, GIFT-Eval, and TIME.
Architecture + recipe infographic: compact diagram showing the shared architecture, core hyperparameters, and training data sources.
Robustness vignette: before/after visualization showing performance on clean vs contaminated time series (demonstrating TIME benchmark gains).
paper_title: Toto 2.0: Time Series Forecasting Enters the Scaling Era
paper_authors: Emaad Khwaja, Chris Lettieri, Gerald Woo, Eden Belouadah, Marc Cenac
